chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
There is no justice in passing a verdict by relying on probability.

key_terms.الثِّقَةِ: The trustworthy person (one whose testimony is accepted)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between justice and certainty in Islamic judicial rulings?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the high standard of justice required in judicial verdicts and the lower threshold of probability (ظن) acceptable in general matters. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that a judge's ruling must be based on firm evidence or certainty to prevent injustice, as relying on mere suspicion undermines the integrity of the legal process. The statement underscores the gravity of judicial authority, where the presumption of innocence is maintained until definitive proof is established.
